newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Six go on trial for Bangladesh leader's murder.
newsitem.headline: Six go on trial for Bangladesh leader's murder.

text.p: The alleged killers of Bangladesh's independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman were formally charged at a special court in Dhaka on Sunday with murder, conspiracy and concealing evidence.
Five of the six accused appeared in court at the resumption of their trial, four ex-army officers who have been in police custody for months, and Mujib's information minister Taheruddin Thakur.
Zobaida Rashid, wife of co-accused retired colonel Shahriar Rashid, failed to appear because she had been ill, her lawyer told the court.
Mujib, father of Bangladesh's current Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, was killed in an army coup in August 1975. He led Bangladesh, formerly East Pakistan, to independence from Pakistan in 1971.
His alleged killers could not be put on trial until Hasina took office last June because his successors passed a law protecting the masterminds of the 1975 coup from legal action.
Bangladesh's parliament repealed the so-called "black law" in November.
Fourteen other people accused of involvement in Mujib's assassination, mostly retired army men, have gone into hiding and several are believed to have left the country.
The trial will continue on Monday.
